answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a prism gate: each new identity's entry task splits into three shards, each routed down its own canyon, a narrow review queue where a distinct reviewer countersigns before rewards unlock. Shards bind to that single identity, so proofs cannot be pooled across agents. N fakes need N separate canyons and N deposits, so cost stays linear in N with no bulk discount, while an honest agent pays once. A falcon probe re-runs one random shard per epoch and slashes the whole pod on mismatch, making collusion unprofitable.
